A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreeCure. Their complete main texts and appendices, including rendered figures, tables and equations, support comparison. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation evaluations, component ablations, attention analyses and noise-robustness experiments in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds model comparisons, mask-robustness and non-facial evaluations, runtime measurements and a 30-participant user study.

M1.justification: The dual-denoising, FASA and APG pipeline remains. Section 4.1 adds a targeted FASA adaptation for FLUX joint visual/textual attention, selectively incorporating FD visual keys and values with a block mask. This changes the attention procedure without replacing the central method.

E1.justification: The 50-identity facial benchmark is retained. Appendix A.3.5 adds non-facial object and clothing prompts using PuLID's prompt set, while A.4.2 introduces deliberately inaccurate mask conditions. These extend existing personalization coverage without adding a new identity dataset.

E2.justification: The evaluated method set expands from five to seven through InstantID and InfiniteYou, including their participation in main, multi-attribute and component comparisons. InstantID was previously only cited. The original five methods remain; PuLID is additionally evaluated with a FLUX configuration.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include FLUX configurations, a 30-participant study using ten samples per baseline, and 25-pixel mask dilation/erosion. Table 6 also replaces 'sunglasses and silver earrings' with 'sunglasses, frowning worriedly'. This is a reported prompt-setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds quantitative mask-accuracy robustness tests, cross-baseline hyperparameter-range analysis and runtime analysis. Table 11 adds PC/IF measurements to existing cross-attention interpolation examples, without establishing a finer interpolation grid. Original noise, non-interference and U-Net placement analyses remain, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both report 20 generated images per identity-prompt pair. v3 adds no seed or repeated-run documentation, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests. Its new foundation-model averages and user-study percentages remain point summaries.

E6.justification: The original five baselines' Table 1 scores are unchanged, and former Tables 2–3 survive within appendix Tables 7 and 10. New results cover InstantID/FLUX, non-facial attributes, mask errors, interpolation, user preferences and runtime. For example, v3 reports PuLID-FLUX PC of 22.42 without and 24.78 with FreeCure.

T1.justification: v3 adds the mathematical definition of FLUX FASA and its joint-attention block mask in Equations 5–6. The original self-attention formulation remains. This is a limited formal extension; neither version provides theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract removes its U-Net-specific framing and explicitly claims compatibility with both Stable Diffusion and FLUX. The central contributions—training-free attribute restoration, non-interfering enhancement and preservation of identity fidelity—remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds concrete limitations involving transparent objects, attribute entanglement and unexplored autoregressive applicability. It also explains weaker non-facial improvements, failures caused by eroded masks, and the tradeoff between training-free operation and increased inference cost. These substantially expand v2's discussion of applicability and limitations.

D1.justification: v3 expands baseline-specific identity-disabling instructions, discloses H800/80GB hardware and 30/50-step timing settings, and supplies the 1–10 user-rating questionnaire. Appendix A.1 adds dataset provenance/licensing information and a stated release policy restricted to accredited researchers. These are substantial documentation additions.

R1.justification: Related Work substantially expands its treatment of adapters, DiT personalization and attention-based editing, adding works including InfiniteYou, OminiControl, Add-it and Nested Attention. It replaces the earlier latent-space editing discussion with positioning around object-level versus fine-grained facial control, and explicitly relates FLUX masking to OminiControl.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain. Related Work and portions of the motivation, method explanation and results discussion are rewritten or condensed; appendix material is reorganized, and author affiliations and conference front matter are updated.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column layout, merges earlier figures, expands and splits qualitative comparison grids, and adds user-study plots and analysis tables. Main Tables 2–3 now summarize results by foundation model, with method-level results moved into the appendix. This substantially reorganizes the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for practical applicability: FLUX evaluations support the architectural extension, mask perturbations test a critical dependency, and human ratings supplement automated metrics. Runtime measurements and concrete failure conditions make costs and limitations assessable where v2 was silent. Uncertainty reporting remains absent, but the added validation and transparency provide a substantial overall quality gain.
